**Grant Application: Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC) for CalVIP Funding**

Sacramento's communities of color face alarmingly high rates of gun violence, demanding culturally competent and innovative prevention strategies. Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, requests $500,000 from CalVIP to implement critical gun violence prevention and safety education. Existing programs often miss the mark; our mission is to fill this critical gap by empowering residents with knowledge and conflict resolution skills, directly addressing violence drivers.

Our innovative strategy includes "Gloxsie 21," a cartoon IP teaching foundational gun safety through relatable storytelling for youth, fostering responsible attitudes from an early age. We also offer AI education, providing critical tech literacy and future pathway opportunities that reduce desperation, a known violence predictor. Alongside, community workshops, in partnership with the esteemed Church of Legacy, facilitate open dialogues on safe gun storage, conflict de-escalation, and mental wellness.

Funding will lead to measurable reductions in accidental shootings, increased awareness of responsible firearm practices, and enhanced community resilience against violence. As a minority-owned organization deeply rooted in Sacramento, GAFC possesses unparalleled credibility and cultural fluency. Our authentic approach, coupled with the trusted presence of Church of Legacy, ensures programs resonate and create lasting change. We are uniquely positioned to transform gun safety education into true violence prevention.
